**Test image key features:**
- Stem at the soil line, split longitudinally (cut open for diagnosis)
- Pale/bleached white interior tissue
- White material coating the stem exterior
- Completely collapsed/dead plant
- Sandy soil background
- Fibrous roots visible at top

**Comparison against reference images:**

- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (stem, 1572830): Shows white cottony mycelium surrounding the stem with dark sclerotia — the white exterior matches. KB description specifically says "positive identification achieved by slicing the diseased stem longitudinally" and "bleached and hardened" stem — this matches the split stem with pale interior in the test image almost exactly.
- **Southern_Blight** (stem, 1575059): Shows dark brown canker lesion — doesn't match the white appearance in the test image. The whole_plant reference (1575058) shows the sandy soil and collapsed plant context, but no white mycelium detail visible.
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt** (stem, 1568041): Shows brown discoloration in pith — the interior is brown, not pale white like the test image.
- All other classes (Alternaria, Bacterial_Wilt, Gray_Mold, Rhizopus, Anthracnose, Bacterial_Canker, Late_Blight, Early_Blight, Verticillium, Septoria, TSWV): Do not match the white-coated stem/pale interior pattern.

The bleached interior revealed by longitudinal stem splitting, combined with white mycelium on the exterior, is the hallmark of **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**.
